sources.entry: langchain - A framework for building agents and LLM-powered applications.
LangChain — One of the most widely used frameworks for building LLM-powered agents and chains. Extensive integrations. Raised $125M at $1.25B valuation (Oct 2025). MIT.

summary.one_liner: LangChain is a framework for building LLM-powered agents and applications by chaining together interoperable components and third-party integrations.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes LangChain as a framework for building agents and LLM-powered applications, focused on chaining together interoperable components and third-party integrations. It provides a standard interface for chat models, embeddings, vector stores, retrievers, tools, and toolkits, so models can be swapped without rewriting the application. The quickstart shows installing with uv and calling a chat model through init_chat_model. The README positions the framework alongside related products: LangGraph for lower-level agent orchestration, Deep Agents for higher-level agents with planning and subagents, and LangSmith for evals, observability, and debugging. A LangChain.js library is mentioned as the JS/TS equivalent.
use_cases: connect LLMs to external data sources
notable: Standard interface for models, embeddings, and vector stores that allows swapping providers
Large ecosystem of third-party integrations for model providers, tools, vector stores, and retrievers
Layered abstractions from high-level chains to low-level components
Part of a suite with LangGraph, Deep Agents, and LangSmith
caveats: Advanced orchestration is delegated to the separate LangGraph product
Production monitoring and debugging rely on the separate LangSmith product
